hook.line: In the café, news travels faster than the espresso. Don Hernando always opens with one of two questions: have you ever come across something, or have you just heard some news? Spanish keeps these apart.
hook.en: Did you hear they closed the street?

examples.en: Have you heard of Botero? (to a friend)

examples.es: No he oído hablar de ese barrio.
examples.en: I haven't heard of that neighbourhood.
I heard they closed the bakery.

examples.es: ¿Supiste que Laura se va a casar?
examples.en: Did you hear Laura is getting married? (to a friend)
Did you see that Altamira bought another building? (to a friend)

examples.es: Hernando oyó que van a cerrar el café.
examples.en: Hernando heard they're going to close the café.

rule:
Two ways to say *heard*, for two jobs.

*Oír hablar de* + a noun: have you come across it at all? Use the perfect for this experience. *¿Has oído hablar de Botero?*

*Oír que* + a full sentence: fresh news. *Oí que cerraron la panadería.*

For asking about news, Latin Americans reach for the past: *¿Supiste que...?* or *¿Viste que...?*, not the perfect. Say *¿Supiste que cerraron la calle?*

After *que*, the news is a normal sentence with no change.
smallPrint: Teachers call *oír hablar de* an experience phrase; *supiste que* and *viste que* are news openers.

options: Have you heard of Botero?
Did you hear Botero called?
Have you heard Botero speak?

I heard the bakery owner speak.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *que*: Oí ___ cerraron la panadería.
yourTurn.why: A full sentence of news follows, so *que*.
A name or thing follows, so *hablar de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Have you heard of Botero? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Have you ever come across him: the perfect, plus *hablar de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Did you hear they closed the street? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: News in Latin America opens with the past: *supiste que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I heard Altamira bought the building.
yourTurn.answer: Oí que Altamira compró el edificio.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I haven't heard of that neighbourhood.
yourTurn.answer: No he oído hablar de ese barrio.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a question about news: Laura se va a casar. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Supiste que Laura se va a casar?
accept: ¿Viste que Laura se va a casar?
yourTurn.why: Open with *supiste que* and keep the news as is.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Has oído hablar que cerraron la calle?
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Hablar de* goes with a thing; a whole piece of news takes *oí que* or *supiste que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Oí hablar que Altamira compró el edificio.
pitfalls.right: Oí que Altamira compró el edificio.
pitfalls.why: Drop *hablar*: for news you just need *oí que*.
English says *heard of*; Spanish keeps the little word *de*.

personal: Tell a friend a piece of news you heard this week, starting with *Oí que...*, or ask about someone famous with *¿Has oído hablar de...?*
